title: Relative ordered root products and the multiplication open cell
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $H$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme whose geometric fibres are reductive: each is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $S\hookrightarrow H$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], with a specified isomorphism $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$, $r\geq0$, whose geometric fibres are maximal tori; a torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$, and maximal means maximal for subgroup inclusion. Here $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$, with multiplication of units.
Let $M=\mathbf Z^r$ and let $\Phi$, $\Phi^+$ and $U_\alpha$ be root data and root subgroups supplied by [lem-sfb-local-split-root-data-weyl-lifts] for this $H,S$: $\Phi$ is the nonzero character-weight set in the tangent module, $\Phi^+$ is the subset positive for an integer linear functional nonzero on $\Phi$, and $U_\alpha\simeq\mathbf G_{a,A}$ is the root subgroup for $\alpha$. Set $N=|\Phi^+|$. Multiplication, in any enumeration without repetitions, identifies $\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}U_\alpha$ and $\prod_{\alpha\in-\Phi^+}U_\alpha$ with smooth closed $A$-subgroups $U^+$ and $U^-$ of $H$. They are normalized by $S$. Multiplication identifies $S\times_AU^+$ with a closed subgroup $B\subseteq H$, with the semidirect product group law given by conjugation. Over every algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, $B_F$ is a Borel subgroup (a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup), $(U^+)_F$ is its unipotent radical (largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup), and its roots are $\Phi^+$; $(U^-)_F$ is the radical of the opposite Borel, with roots $-\Phi^+$. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. The multiplication morphism
$$j:U^-\times_AS\times_AU^+\longrightarrow H,\qquad(v,s,u)\longmapsto vsu$$
is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. These products, subgroup inclusions, and the displayed open immersion commute with base change. Empty products are $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 5.1.13 and proof, printed pp.143-144 (ordered positive root products, closed Borel and relative open cell), with Theorem 4.1.4 for root parametrizations. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. Geometric Borel terminology agrees with Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), 21.32 and 21.68.

proof.text: Write $\ell:M\to\mathbf Z$ for the functional defining $\Phi^+$. The specified split torus gives a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to S$ by $z_j\mapsto t^{\ell(e_j)}$; the root formula in [lem-sfb-local-split-root-data-weyl-lifts] gives $\alpha(\lambda(t))=t^{\ell(\alpha)}$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] to conjugation through $\lambda$, and to $-\lambda$, in $H$. Finite type over the Noetherian ring gives finite presentation: in any finite polynomial presentation its kernel is a finitely generated ideal. Obtain smooth closed groups $U_\pm,P_\pm,Z$, with $P_+=Z\ltimes U_+$, connected geometric fibres and unipotent fibres for $U_\pm$. Their construction is by the explicit graded coordinate ideals of that node, not by schematic closure of geometric points.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, first paragraph, and Theorem 4.1.7

proof.text: The torus $S$ centralizes $\lambda$, so its inclusion in $H$ factors through $Z$. On each algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, $\lambda_F$ is regular since every $\ell(\alpha)$ is nonzero. The final assertion of [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] gives $Z_{H_F}(\lambda_F)=S_F$. The base-change statement of [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] identifies this centralizer with $Z_F$. Apply the isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] to $S\to Z$: its geometric fibres are these isomorphisms; $S$ is smooth (Laurent variables lift across square-zero quotients), and $Z$ is smooth. Both are affine finite type over Noetherian $A$, so this map is finitely presented. Hence $S=Z$ as subgroup schemes. Put $B=P_+$ and $U^\pm=U_\pm$. The dynamic semidirect-product isomorphism now gives $S\times_AU^+\simeq B$ and the closedness and smoothness of these subgroups. Elements of $S$ commute with $\lambda(t)$, so conjugating any orbit extension by $s\in S$ preserves its limit $1$; this proves $S$-normalization of $U^\pm$ on every test algebra.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, first paragraph: identify Z with T; closedness from the dynamic construction

proof.text: Over an algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] identifies $B_F=P(\lambda_F)$ as a Borel with positive roots $\Phi^+$, and $P(-\lambda_F)$ as the Borel with negative roots, hence the opposite Borel relative to $S_F$. Let $R=R_u(B_F)$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. The dynamic node gives a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup $U^+_F\subset B_F$, hence $U^+_F\subset R$ by maximality. The projection $q:B_F\to S_F$ from the dynamic semidirect product kills $R$ by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], so $R\subset\ker q=U^+_F$. Thus $R=U^+_F$ as subgroup schemes, not just on $F$-points. Apply the same argument to $-\lambda$ for $U^-_F$.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, last paragraph: geometric Borels and their unipotent radicals

proof.text: For $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, the root formula gives $\lambda(t)u_\alpha(c)\lambda(t)^{-1}=u_\alpha(t^{\ell(\alpha)}c)$. The right side is a polynomial in $t$ and has value $1$ at $0$ since $\ell(\alpha)>0$. This identity over every $A$-algebra proves $U_\alpha\subset U^+$ by the defining functor of the dynamic node. Replacing $\lambda$ by $-\lambda$ proves $U_\alpha\subset U^-$ for $\alpha\in-\Phi^+$. Thus multiplication defines a morphism $m_\pm$ from each ordered product of the corresponding root groups into $U^\pm$. This establishes factorization on nonreduced test algebras as well.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, middle paragraph: root inclusions by positive scaling

proof.text: Fix any enumeration, without changing it. On every algebraically closed geometric fibre, step 3 identifies $U^\pm_F$ with the relevant Borel radical; the root subgroups are the geometric root subgroups by [lem-sfb-local-split-root-data-weyl-lifts]. Therefore [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] identifies $(m_\pm)_F$ as an isomorphism, in this precise order. The source is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ through the root parametrizations: it is finitely presented and formally smooth since its variables lift independently across any square-zero quotient. The target $U^\pm$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups]. Each $m_\pm$ is finitely presented since both affine schemes are finite type over Noetherian $A$. The isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] consequently makes each $m_\pm$ an isomorphism over $A$. This proves the ordered-product assertions, and all orders give the same dynamic closed subgroup.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, last paragraph: fibrewise ordered products and fibral isomorphism criterion

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups], multiplication $U_-\times_AP_+\to H$ is an open immersion. Insert the already established isomorphism $S\times_AU^+\simeq P_+$ and $U_-=U^-$: this gives exactly $(v,s,u)\mapsto vsu$ and proves the required open immersion $j$. There is no further spreading argument. For an arbitrary $A\to A'$, the graded coordinate ideals defining $P_\pm,U_\pm,Z$ generate their scalar-extended ideals, as asserted by the same node. Thus these base changes are the dynamic subgroups of $H_{A'}$. Multiplication, inclusion, projection and the root product maps are base changes of the original group morphisms, and the inverse root-coordinate and semidirect-product isomorphisms also base change. Hence all products and the open cell commute with arbitrary and successive base change. If $\Phi$ is empty, step 5 has source $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and gives $U^\pm=1$ and $B=S$; the open immersion is the corresponding unit-factor map. A rank-zero torus forces the root set empty; none of the arguments excludes this case.

R_u(B_F) = U⁺_F follows from maximality in one direction and from unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial in the other. (4) U_α lies in U⁺ by the polynomial t^{ℓ(α)}c on every test algebra. (5) Ordered root products are isomorphisms: borel-root-product-coordinates on fibres, then the fibre criterion (source A^N is flat and lfp, A is Noetherian so maps are lfp).
